decisions.reason: As a close-to-core decorative arch that was featured prominently for two years, it likely has low carrying cost and still fits the firm's premium seasonal range better than a full withdrawal.
This one-tier Christmas pyramid is very close to the firm's established craft business, so continued assortment breadth is likely worth more than the small cost of keeping it.

The electronic music box was a more distant experiment, and after several seasons the uncertainty about its fit has likely resolved enough that management would reallocate effort toward core handcrafted lines.
Although it received a second edition, this motif platform depends on the distant electronic music-box concept and is therefore more likely to be cut when the firm rationalizes a broad portfolio.
This seasonal electronic add-on is both distant from the firm's traditional strengths and narrowly themed, so its option value is likely lower than the benefit of freeing resources for core products.
A Dresden-themed Christmas pyramid builds directly on the firm's established premium collectible offer, making it a plausible niche variant to retain within the assortment.
